work.title: Water Music, Suite No. 2 in D

version.value: Performing edition not identified. The movement number (13 of the three suites) and the strains heard (a first strain of 8 bars and a second of 16, each played twice) match the Hallische Händel-Ausgabe text. The recording then plays all 24 bars once more without repeats, which that edition does not print; no editor or continuo realisation is credited.
version.note: The programme and Commons name the work and movement numbers but no edition. The Hallische Händel-Ausgabe (Redlich, 1962) prints 24 bars with a repeat sign after bar 8 and after bar 24 and no da capo; the second statement follows from the measured pauses (about 54 s for 24 bars at the first statement’s pace) and is a feature of this performance. Commons and the candidate list place this movement fifth in the suite; the edition numbers it third (13), and Arnold’s 1788 score prints it last, headed Coro.

value.name: Marine Chamber Orchestra, United States Marine Band

performers.note: Commons gives the conductor as Major Michelle Rakers; the programme prints Major Michelle A. Rakers. No roster of individual players is published in the consulted sources. The video’s closing frames show the whole orchestra standing; the ensemble’s harpsichord, bassoon and trumpet are visible in the other movements’ videos, and no frame shows horns or oboes. Which sections play in each statement is not established: an independent look at the official video reports upper-string players resting at about 1:05, where the printed score gives them notes, so the recording is not assumed to follow the printed parts. No orchestra view is authored for this movement for that reason.

date.note: Commons gives performance_date 2017-01-29; the programme prints Sunday, January 29, 2017 at 2:00 P.M.; the official video description repeats the date. This Minuet is the last item of the programme. The Commons composition_date field, 1717-07-17, is the date of the documented first performance on the Thames, not a composition date.

place.value: Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center, Northern Virginia Community College, Alexandria Campus, Alexandria, Virginia, United States
place.note: Commons says Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, VA; the programme gives the full name of the hall and campus.

label.note: No record label is identified. The source is an official concert video on the Marine Band’s YouTube channel; the channel is not treated as a label, and no commercial release was found.

catalogue.note: Born-digital concert video. The YouTube video ID fRhxYQOWkX0 identifies the source video but is not a catalogue number.

matrixTakeSides.note: A concert recording made in digital form has no matrix, take or side numbers.

credits.note: No transfer or mastering engineer is identified. The Commons file history shows the batch upload by the user Mysterymanblue (pattypan), which is an uploader credit, not an engineering credit.

date.note: No transfer date is documented. The YouTube publication date (30 April 2018) and the Commons upload date (28 June 2021) are not session or transfer dates.

processing.value: Opus audio file (48 kHz, two channels, encoder Lavf58.29.100) listed on Commons with the Marine Band’s YouTube playlist as its source; Commons supplies an MP3 access derivative. The file keeps the audience’s applause after the last chord.
processing.note: The file’s own metadata documents the Opus format and encoder. That the audio was taken from the official video’s sound track is inferred from the source field and from the matching title and duration (195 s); the processing chain is not described. That the closing half-minute is applause is inferred from its sound and from the standing players and audience silhouettes in the video’s last frames.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Opus

composition.value: Handel (died 1759): the composition is in the public domain.
composition.note: Commons tags the composition PD-old-auto-expired (death year 1759). The performing edition is not identified; editorial copyright in a modern edition, if one was used, is separate from the sound recording.

recording.value: Commons tags the performance and recording PD-USGov-Military-Marines: a work of a United States Marine or employee made as part of official duties, public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government.
recording.note: This is a U.S.-jurisdiction statement, not a claim of worldwide status. The programme carries a general notice that a performance may contain third-party material and should not be assumed to be public domain; no third-party material is identified in this performance of a composition from before 1759, but the notice is recorded here. The official Marine Band YouTube channel published the source video.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 50–51 (movement 13, bars 1–24): first strain bars 1–8 and second strain bars 9–24, each closed by a repeat sign; trumpets and horns resting in bars 9–11; the final bar a dotted minim in every part. Consulted for bar numbering only; its copyright status in the United States is not established and it is not the stated score source of the orchestra view.
